summary: The note surveys the surge of digital art platforms since September 2023, arguing they democratize the art market, use blockchain and smart contracts to secure authenticity and artist earnings, and apply AI curation. It also covers platforms focused on protecting rights, fair trade and social causes, citing specific platforms, launch dates and artists.
one_line: Digital art platforms launched since late 2023 are democratizing art distribution through blockchain, smart contracts, AI curation, ethical trading and social-cause partnerships.
key_facts: Visionary Pixels launched on October 15th, 2023, and helped emerging artists Zoe Ramirez and Eliot Wu reach a global audience.
As of November 2023, Artiverse had democratized access to the art market, letting emerging artists compete with established names.
Artiverse CEO Samantha Chung said on December 1st, 2023: "We're stripping away the gatekeepers."
Michael Torres' work "Ether Dreams" was the first sold as an NFT on ArtChain, which launched on September 20th, 2023.
Blockchain's immutable, transparent ledger serves as a record of ownership and provenance for digital art.
Smart contracts are self-executing contracts with terms written in code; they changed the earnings model for creators.
Sofia Karpov earns a percentage each time "The Abyss of Thoughts" is traded on Digital Easel, which debuted on November 12th, 2023.
CurateAI, which debuted on December 25th, 2023, uses AI to match artist profiles with audience preferences, boosting artists like Juan Delgado, whose animated landscapes found a niche.
PixelSafe, known for state-of-the-art encryption, hosted an international digital art showcase on January 18th, 2024.
Sarah Jenkins said on March 7th, 2024, that platforms like ArtEthics ensure a fairness standard in the industry.
Artivists launched on February 14th, 2024, promotes artists like Ava Johnson, whose 3D-modelled sculptures address climate change.
Artivists partners with organizations to direct a portion of sales toward cause-related actions.
